answers.name: Apple
answers.fact: There are over 7,500 apple varieties.

answers.name: Banana
answers.fact: Botanically a berry. Strawberries aren't.

answers.name: Orange
answers.fact: The colour was named after the fruit, not the other way round.

answers.name: Strawberry
answers.fact: Wears its seeds on the outside.

answers.name: Grape
answers.fact: Grown by people for around 8,000 years.

answers.name: Mango
answers.fact: India grows more mangoes than anywhere else.

answers.name: Pineapple
answers.fact: Takes about two years to grow one.

answers.name: Watermelon
answers.fact: About 92% water.

answers.name: Pear
answers.fact: Ripens best off the tree.

answers.name: Cherry
answers.fact: Japan celebrates cherry blossom season with hanami.

answers.name: Peach
answers.fact: From China, despite a Latin name meaning 'Persian'.

answers.name: Lemon
answers.fact: A hybrid of bitter orange and citron.

answers.name: Durian
answers.fact: So smelly it's banned on Singapore's public transport.

answers.name: Dragon fruit
answers.fact: Grows on a climbing cactus.

answers.name: Kiwi fruit
answers.fact: Originally called the Chinese gooseberry.

answers.name: Blueberry
answers.fact: One of the few fruits native to North America.

answers.name: Raspberry
answers.fact: Each one is a cluster of tiny fruits called drupelets.

answers.name: Blackberry
answers.fact: Also called a bramble.

answers.name: Plum
answers.fact: Dried, it becomes a prune.

answers.name: Apricot
answers.fact: Dried apricots go dark brown unless treated.

answers.name: Nectarine
answers.fact: Basically a peach without the fuzz.

answers.name: Lime
answers.fact: British sailors ate them against scurvy: hence 'limeys'.

answers.name: Grapefruit
answers.fact: Can interfere with some medicines.

answers.name: Mandarin
answers.fact: An easy-peel citrus, and an ancestor of the orange.

answers.name: Tangerine
answers.fact: Named after Tangier in Morocco.

answers.name: Clementine
answers.fact: Usually seedless, and a winter favourite.

answers.name: Coconut
answers.fact: Technically a drupe, not a nut.

answers.name: Papaya
answers.fact: Usually called pawpaw in Australia.

answers.name: Passionfruit
answers.fact: Named by missionaries who saw Christian symbols in its flower.

answers.name: Pomegranate
answers.fact: Packed with hundreds of seeds.

answers.name: Fig
answers.fact: Most figs are pollinated by a tiny wasp.

answers.name: Date
answers.fact: Grown in the Middle East for thousands of years.

answers.name: Lychee
answers.fact: Translucent flesh under a bumpy red shell.

answers.name: Avocado
answers.fact: A berry with one big seed.

answers.name: Tomato
answers.fact: Botanically a fruit.

answers.name: Cantaloupe
answers.fact: Called rockmelon in Australia.

answers.name: Honeydew
answers.fact: A pale green melon.

answers.name: Cranberry
answers.fact: Ripe ones bounce.

answers.name: Guava
answers.fact: Has more vitamin C than an orange.

answers.name: Persimmon
answers.fact: Some kinds pucker your mouth until they're fully soft.

answers.name: Starfruit
answers.fact: Slice it and you get perfect stars.

answers.name: Jackfruit
answers.fact: The largest tree fruit, weighing up to around 40 kg.

answers.name: Rambutan
answers.fact: Its name comes from the Malay word for 'hair'.

answers.name: Mangosteen
answers.fact: Nicknamed the 'queen of fruits'.

answers.name: Kumquat
answers.fact: You eat it whole, skin and all.

answers.name: Quince
answers.fact: Too hard and sour to eat raw, so it's cooked into paste.

answers.name: Gooseberry
answers.fact: Tart little berries, often cooked into fools and pies.

answers.name: Blackcurrant
answers.fact: Banned in the US for decades over a plant disease.

answers.name: Mulberry
answers.fact: Silkworms eat its leaves.

answers.name: Olive
answers.fact: Technically a fruit.

answers.name: Plantain
answers.fact: A starchy cooking banana.

answers.name: Redcurrant
answers.fact: Tart red berries that grow in strings.

answers.name: Elderberry
answers.fact: Should be cooked first: raw ones can upset your stomach.

answers.name: Tamarind
answers.fact: A sour pod used in pad thai and Worcestershire sauce.

answers.name: Soursop
answers.fact: A spiky green fruit with creamy flesh.

answers.name: Feijoa
answers.fact: A New Zealand favourite with a fragrant, minty-sweet taste.

answers.name: Loquat
answers.fact: A small orange fruit from China, related to apples.

answers.name: Longan
answers.fact: 'Dragon eye' in Chinese.

answers.name: Ugli fruit
answers.fact: A Jamaican tangelo.

answers.name: Pomelo
answers.fact: The biggest citrus fruit.

answers.name: Boysenberry
answers.fact: A raspberry, blackberry and loganberry cross.

answers.name: Loganberry
answers.fact: An accidental raspberry–blackberry cross from California.

answers.name: Cherimoya
answers.fact: Mark Twain called it 'deliciousness itself'.

answers.name: Salak
answers.fact: Its skin looks like snakeskin.

answers.name: Ackee
answers.fact: Jamaica's national fruit.

answers.name: Breadfruit
answers.fact: Captain Bligh was carrying breadfruit plants when the Bounty mutiny hit.

answers.name: Physalis
answers.fact: Comes wrapped in a papery husk.

answers.name: Buddha's hand
answers.fact: A citrus shaped like fingers, almost all peel.

answers.name: Yuzu
answers.fact: A tart Japanese citrus.

answers.name: Medlar
answers.fact: Eaten only once it's half-rotten, or 'bletted'.

answers.name: Kakadu plum
answers.fact: An Australian bush food packed with vitamin C.

answers.name: Quandong
answers.fact: An Australian desert 'peach'.

answers.name: Jabuticaba
answers.fact: Grows straight out of the tree's trunk.

answers.name: Miracle fruit
answers.fact: Makes sour food taste sweet for a while.

answers.name: Cupuaçu
answers.fact: A Brazilian cousin of cacao.

answers.name: Finger lime
answers.fact: Australia's 'citrus caviar', full of tiny juice pearls.
